summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman was admitted for acute on chronic lower extremity edema worsened over several weeks, unresponsive to oral diuretics. She was started on IV furosemide via a PICC line after initial placement and repositioning confirmed by imaging. Echocardiogram showed preserved systolic function, supporting lymphedema or venous stasis as the cause. The hospital course was complicated by a generalized seizure, likely triggered by volume overload, prompting an increase in levetiracetam dose despite therapeutic levels. IV diuresis was stopped due to a slight rise in creatinine, and she was transitioned to higher-dose oral bumetanide. Her warfarin was uptitrated to achieve a therapeutic INR. Leukocytosis persisted without infection. She was discharged home with increased diuretic and seizure medication, instructions for weight monitoring, and follow-up in primary care, neurology, and an outpatient diuretic clinic.
